quizName: DMV Practice Test #10 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, what formation should riders use?
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation on straightaways. However, switch to single-file when going through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If you must brake and swerve to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
Brake and swerve at the same time.
Choose to either brake or swerve.
Not swerve and only use the front brake to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Either brake then swerve or swerve then brake.
questions.explanation: Do the actions one after the other, not at the same time. Braking and swerving together can cause your motorcycle to tip over.

questions.question: What should you wear when riding a motorcycle?

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it's warm out.
Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
Not be concerned about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. A jacket protects you and helps prevent dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: Which sign is rectangular in shape?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular, white, and have black lettering. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: What must you have to carry a passenger on a motorcycle?

options.text: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only have one set of footrests.
Not encourage the passenger to wear protective clothing.
Put a sticker on the brake light to warn other motorists that a passenger is on the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have a seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat designed for two riders and footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that you wear.

questions.question: What should you do if your motorcycle starts to wobble?

options.text: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the handlebars firmly and close the throttle gradually.
questions.explanation: Hold the handlebars firmly and slowly close the throttle to slow down. Move your weight forward and down. Pull off the road as soon as possible. Do not speed up or brake, as these actions can make the wobble worse.

questions.question: What should you know about a windshield?

options.text: Is a good substitute for a face shield.
Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not completely protect your eyes from the wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield cannot replace goggles or a face shield. Most windshields do not fully protect your eyes from the wind.

questions.question: What is the best lane position for a motorcycle?

options.text: There is no single best lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is no single best lane position.
questions.explanation: Change your lane position based on road and traffic conditions. Choose a position that gives you the most space and makes other drivers see you better.

questions.question: What does eye contact with a driver really mean?

options.text: Guarantees that they will yield to you.
Doesn't mean that they see you.
Is not worth the effort it takes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doesn't mean that they see you.
questions.explanation: Do not count on eye contact to keep you safe. A driver may look right at you and still not see you.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest and is operated with your left foot. Lift the lever to shift up to a higher gear. Press it down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: What should passengers do?

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.

questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to lean with you when turning. They should hold onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: What does a leather jacket do?

options.text: Is too warm to wear while riding.
Should never be worn while riding.

questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved leather jacket for protection. Leather jackets can help protect you from dehydration in warm weather. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: Which is NOT a safe way to prevent fatigue while riding?

options.text: Protecting yourself from wind, cold, and rain

questions.explanation: Take frequent breaks and do not ride more than six hours in one day. Dress to protect yourself from wind, cold, and rain. Avoid artificial stimulants because they can be dangerous when they wear off.

questions.question: What is allowed in a no passing zone?

options.text: A motorcycle may pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
A motorcycle may pass if it finishes before another vehicle approaches.
A motorcycle may pass on the shoulder.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle cannot pass another vehicle.
questions.explanation: Passing is not allowed in no passing zones. You also cannot pass by riding off the main road.

questions.question: When adjusting mirrors, what should you focus on?

options.text: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
The road in front of your motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road behind and beside your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors to see the lane behind you and the lane beside you. A properly adjusted mirror may show the edge of your arm or shoulder, but the road behind and beside you is most important.

questions.question: How should you swerve?

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to go.
Press the handgrip in the opposite direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction you want to go.
questions.explanation: To swerve, press the handgrip on the side where you want to go. To swerve left, press the left handgrip, then press the right to recover. To swerve right, press the right handgrip, then the left.

questions.question: Why is riding directly alongside another vehicle dangerous?

options.text: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
It is safer than riding behind the vehicle.
It is safe because it limits your escape routes.
It should only be done during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Do not ride directly alongside another vehicle. You may be in the driver's blind spot, and they may not see you. If the driver cannot see you, they may move into your lane without warning. Riding alongside also blocks your escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: When riding at night, compared to riding during the day, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Allow more space between you and other vehicles.
Use your high beam whenever possible.

questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase your distance from other vehicles. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther down the road. Be flexible about your lane position when riding at night.

questions.question: What gives a rider the best protection?
questions.explanation: A plastic face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles protect only your eyes. A windshield or eyeglasses do not provide the same protection as goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: What happens when your rear tire skids?

options.text: You lose your ability to change direction.
It is only a problem if the front tire skids too.

questions.correctAnswerText: You lose your ability to change direction.
questions.explanation: A skidding rear tire is dangerous and can cause a serious crash. Too much rear brake pressure locks the rear wheel. When the rear wheel locks, you cannot change direction. Release the brake to regain control.

questions.question: Which of the following should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you avoid other drivers' blind spots.
Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you avoid being seen by other drivers.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of other drivers' blind spots and helps you avoid surface hazards. It also shows other drivers your intentions, protects your lane, helps you avoid wind blasts, and gives you an escape route from hazards.

questions.question: Good lane position should NOT:

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots.
Let other drivers share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other drivers share your lane.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see and be seen. It protects you from wind blasts, keeps you out of blind spots, and avoids surface hazards. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and should provide an escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help protect you from serious injury?
questions.explanation: To protect yourself, wear a DOT helmet, face or eye protection, sturdy jacket and long pants, high sturdy boots or shoes to support your ankles, and durable gloves. Ear buds do not provide protection.

questions.question: Where is the horn button usually located on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: Know where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride. The horn button is usually located next to the left handgrip.

questions.question: What type of footwear is best for a motorcycle rider?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy boots or shoes that are high enough to support your ankles. Laced boots are best, but high-top boots or heavy shoes work well. If your boots have long laces, tuck them in securely before riding.

questions.question: When should a rider check their mirrors?

options.text: When slowing down or stopping suddenly

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors when slowing down or stopping, when stopped at an intersection, when changing lanes, and when turning.

questions.question: Are helmets required for motorcycle riders?

options.text: Only for riders with less than two years of experience.

questions.explanation: All motorcycle riders must wear helmets in New Jersey. Riders can be fined for not wearing a helmet.

questions.question: What should riders do when changing lanes?

options.text: Use only their mirrors to check for other vehicles.
Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
Brake hard to let vehicles in their blind spot pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn their head to look for traffic behind them.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like all vehicles. Always turn your head to check for traffic behind you before changing lanes.

questions.question: Who are crashes most likely to happen to?

options.text: Those who know their motorcycle well.
Those who completed a safety course.

questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often to untrained, beginning riders who do not know their motorcycle well.

questions.question: What features should protective boots or shoes have?

options.text: Long laces that are not tucked in.

questions.explanation: Choose boots or heavy shoes that are tall and sturdy enough to cover and support your ankles. Use low heels so they do not catch on rough surfaces. Tuck in long laces so they do not catch on the motorcycle's moving parts.

questions.question: What color is a warning sign?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering. They alert riders to upcoming road hazards.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, how far behind the vehicle ahead should you ride?
questions.explanation: Under good conditions, stay at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead of you. Increase this distance if conditions are poor.

questions.question: How should a group of riders pass another vehicle?

options.text: All at once in a staggered line

questions.explanation: On a two-lane highway, riders must pass one at a time. Each rider waits for the one ahead to safely return to the original lane before beginning to pass.

questions.question: Which type of clothing helps other drivers see you?
questions.explanation: Wear bright, reflective clothing so other drivers can see you easily.

questions.question: What should a face shield allow?
questions.explanation: A face shield should allow air to pass through. An airtight shield causes fogging and blocks your vision. A good shield has no scratches, clear side views, and fastens securely.

questions.question: Which surface gives a motorcycle the best grip?
questions.explanation: Dry pavement offers the best traction. Wet roads, gravel, sand, mud, snow, ice, painted lines, and metal plates are all slippery and dangerous.

questions.question: When does alcohol start to impair your riding?

options.text: At about half the legal limit

questions.explanation: Even one drink affects your riding ability. You can be impaired before reaching the legal limit. Never drink and ride.

questions.question: Where should you ride to be seen in a driver's rearview mirror?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane behind a car. This position appears in the driver's rearview mirror, which they check more often than side mirrors.

questions.question: What should you NOT check before riding?
questions.explanation: Check your fluids, tires, headlight, taillight, turn signals, brake light, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride.

questions.question: How do over-the-counter drugs affect riding?

options.text: They only affect riding if mixed with alcohol
They affect everyone the same way

questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter drugs, prescription medications, and illegal drugs have side effects that impair your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: Where is the greatest risk of accidents between motorcycle riders and other drivers?
questions.explanation: Intersections are where most accidents happen between motorcycles and other vehicles. Riders must be extra careful when entering and passing through intersections.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding side by side?

options.text: A driver pulling in may not see both riders.
Helmet reflections can make it hard for riders to see.
Riding side by side does not give riders enough room to avoid danger.
Left-side riders have trouble exiting the highway.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding side by side does not give riders enough room to avoid danger.
questions.explanation: Group riders should never ride side by side. Riders need enough space around them to turn, stop, or avoid hazards safely.

questions.question: How do most headache, cold, and hay fever medications affect you?

options.text: They make you unable to focus.

questions.explanation: Many medications for headaches, colds, hay fever, allergies, or anxiety can make you drowsy and reduce your ability to ride safely. Always check how a medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: What happens when you brake while riding through a curve?

options.text: It is the same as braking on a straight road.
You have more grip as you lean into the turn.
You may have less grip as you lean into the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have less grip as you lean into the turn.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but you must be very careful. The tires are already using some grip to turn while leaning, so less grip is left for stopping.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright colors and reflective materials at all times to help other drivers see you.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes:
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than six months of experience. Most crashes happen during the day at slow speeds.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is located on the left handlebar of a motorcycle.

questions.question: Are low-speed crashes serious?

options.text: No, they happen so often there is no need to worry.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen at speeds below 30 miles per hour. Even low-speed crashes can cause fatal injuries.

questions.question: In traffic, how much stopping distance does a motorcycle need compared to a car?
questions.explanation: A motorcycle needs the same stopping distance as a car in traffic.

questions.question: Where should inexperienced riders position themselves in a group?

options.text: At the back of the group

questions.explanation: Inexperienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This lets experienced riders watch over them and help if needed.
